summary: The install stick a person installs Rach2 from, and the installer, the raw writer and the recovery system's key on the machines it boots; the scenarios are tests/cases/machine/installer_*.c

cases.behavior: the product's install stick has three partitions, the root image and a manifest of the sealed disk on its volume, boots by USB and by IDE beside a copy of the sealed disk, saves the disk's boot and recovery partitions to its volume, updates the disk's root, requests term twice, boots the changed menu, and writes the saved partitions back whole
units: `tests/system/install_stick_test.sh`, the stick's volume, its boots by USB and by IDE with the update and the saves, the write back, and the checks after them

inputs.sealed: the sealed disk, whose copy the boots write
inputs.root: the root image the update writes

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends each machine and removes the copies of the stick and the sealed disk, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes the files it read off the volume

steps.does: read the stick's volume on the host: the root image, the manifest, and the sealed disk's two partitions
boot the stick by USB and find both images on its volume
boot the stick by IDE, save the disk's boot and recovery partitions to the volume, update the disk's root without changing the menu, request term twice and read what the updates kept and armed
boot the updated candidate through its changed menu and see init start term
boot the stick and zero the saved boot and recovery partitions
boot the stick by IDE again and write the saved partitions back
compare the partitions and the saved copies with the sealed disk's, and check the volume

assertions.checks: the stick's volume checks clean and has the root image, byte for byte
the manifest on the volume names the sealed disk by its file name, of its length and SHA-256
the sealed disk's boot and recovery partitions are each 64 MiB at a mebibyte boundary
the stick boots by USB, and its mounted volume has the sealed disk and the root image at its length
the stick boots by IDE, its volume has room for both partitions, and each is saved to it whole
`rach2-install --update` from the stick keeps the group the root had and removes the file the image lacks
the update leaves recovery as the saved entry and the candidate as the next
an update without --console keeps grub.cfg byte for byte
two --console term updates give each installed-root line one token, keep recovery lines byte for byte, and leave the same menu after the second update
the changed menu boots the candidate and init starts term
both partitions were zeroed on the disk
the last stick boot writes both saved partitions back with reflash
both partitions are again the sealed disk's, byte for byte
the copies saved on the volume are the sealed disk's partitions, byte for byte
the stick's volume checks clean after all boots

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended
`rach2-install --update` has written the root from the stick

native.reason: the case boots the install stick by the firmware, by USB and by IDE, a system image other than the installed one

cases.behavior: on the machine the product's stick boots, reflash writes 32 MiB of the sealed disk to a blank disk with its progress, reads them back to the digest sha256sum takes of the same bytes, and does the same for 2 MiB at a later offset without progress lines
units: `tests/system/suites/installer.sh` row 2, the raw write and its readback

inputs.stick: the product's install stick, under an overlay

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the overlay and the blank disk, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the stick beside the blank disk, write the two extents with reflash and read each back
compare the digests and count the progress lines

assertions.checks: the stick boots, mounts its volume and writes and verifies both extents at the console
the digest reflash reads back of the first 32 MiB is the one sha256sum takes of the bytes sent
the readback of the 2 MiB at 32 MiB is the digest of the bytes written there, and not the first extent's
the write asked for its progress printed at least two progress lines
the write not asked for its progress printed none

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case writes a disk node of a machine the stick boots, beside the stick it booted from

cases.behavior: the installer on a machine with two patterned disks refuses wrong answers and writes nothing until told, installs onto the disk named each time, and the disks it writes boot with the accounts given, answer SSH with them, and boot their recovery systems with the key the install placed, or with SSH off when it placed none
units: `tests/system/suites/installer.sh` rows 3 and 3b, the installer's refusals and the installs onto the second and the first of two disks
`tests/system/suites/installer.sh` row 4, the boot of the installed disk
`tests/system/suites/installer.sh` row 6, the SSH logins on the installed machine
`tests/system/suites/installer.sh` rows 6b and 6c, the recovery system's key placed and not

inputs.stick: the test stick, under an overlay
inputs.image: the 108 MiB disk image the test stick carries
inputs.keyless: the recovery image staged with no key

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends each machine and removes the overlay and the two disks, which it keeps after a failure; the scenario removes the keys and the outputs it made

steps.does: boot the declared Rach2 OpenSSH client and open its framed command channel
fill both disks with the pattern, make the recovery key, boot the stick, answer the installer wrongly until it stops, compare both disks with the pattern, and install onto the second
boot the stick again and install onto the first disk with the recovery key, then compare the disks on the host
boot the second disk alone and log in with the password the install was given
boot the first disk and log in over SSH by password and by key
put the keyless recovery image on the first disk, arm its recovery entry, boot it and log in with the placed key
put the keyless recovery image on the second disk, arm its recovery entry, boot it and probe its SSH port

assertions.checks: the installer names what is wrong with each wrong answer and asks again, refuses a confirmation that is not the disk's name, stops when told, and stops when its answers end before its questions
after the refusals both disks are still the pattern, read whole inside the machine
the install onto the second disk checks the image, reads back what it wrote, writes the table, the accounts and the grown root, and finishes
the first disk is still the pattern, byte for byte, after the install onto the second
the kernel published the new table's partitions
the install onto the first disk, given the recovery key and the recovery system's own authorized keys, finishes and takes the key
the second disk is as the first install left it, byte for byte, after the install onto the first
both disks begin with the image's boot code
the root of the disk told to grow is larger than the root of the one that was not
the second disk boots alone, refuses the image's password, takes the new one, and has the policy, the home and no root keys the install left
the second disk's recovery partition has the archive of its accounts
the first disk boots, root logs in at the console, and its SSH server listens
root logs in over SSH with the password the install was given
the account logs in over SSH with the keys the install was given
the image's demonstration key is refused for root
the machine stays up for the attempts, and its console takes the token written over SSH
the first disk's recovery partition has the public key the install was given
the first disk boots its recovery system from its own menu, and the server listens
the recovery system says it took the key off its partition, since its image has none
root logs in to the recovery system with the placed key
the disk has no mount on it after the key was read
a key the install was not given is refused
the recovery system stays up for the attempts, and its console takes the token written over SSH
the second disk's recovery partition has no key file
the second disk boots its recovery system from its own menu, and two console sessions end
the recovery system says SSH is off, and that it took no key
init started no SSH server by its second test for a key
nothing answers SSH: the forwarded connection is closed or refused, with no server's identification
the recovery system takes the token typed after the probe

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case installs onto the disks of machines the stick boots, and boots the recovery systems of the disks it wrote

units: `tests/system/suites/installer.sh` row 7, the stick whose manifest is spoiled

inputs.stick: a copy of the test stick with one digit of its manifest's hash changed

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes the stick's copy and the disk, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: change one digit of the hash in the manifest of the stick's copy, and fill the disk with the pattern
boot the stick beside the disk, run the installer to its refusal, and compare the disk

assertions.checks: one digit of the hash in the manifest on the stick's copy was changed
the installer finds that the image is not the one the manifest describes, and stops
the disk is still the pattern, byte for byte
